findings.title: Later mandatory proof extensions have no executable campaign allocation
findings.observation: The charter explicitly requires MC04/MC05 to extend the fixed-authority MC03 proof and MC06 to prove additional split/join relations. Its resource table nevertheless permits one native positive campaign containing exactly two financial transitions, and a new campaign requires a new reviewed proposal and explicit user authorization. MC03 is expressly the original accrual/due-settlement episode. MC05 wires those artifacts into acceptance, while MC06 requires real branch proofs. No extension campaign allocation or concrete native prover/relation work product bridges the two.
findings.impact: Even a successful MC03 run cannot satisfy later loan/swap intent and composition predicates under the recorded execution contract. The loop must either stop for a newly planned campaign or exceed the contract; neither constitutes an executable plan to close all seven gaps.
findings.correction: Scope the one-campaign restriction explicitly to MC03 revision-01. Add bounded, separately gated native relation/prover extension tasks and owned artifacts for MC04/MC05, MC06, and any new MC07 relation. Allocate their campaigns, cumulative time/output/k ceilings, positive episodes and meaningful rejection controls within the existing program limits; prohibit automatic retries after failure. Preserve the separate requirement for both auditors to review implemented relations and contracts before launch. If the intended authority only covers MC03, instead explicitly mark later proof execution contingent on a new reviewed allocation and avoid claiming the current loop can execute the whole completion program.
